client_situation.text: The RFP is issued by Empire State Development (ESD), a New York State economic development corporation whose mission is to promote a growing state economy, encourage business investment and job creation, and support diverse local economies through loans, grants, tax credits, real estate development and marketing.

ESD's Office of Strategic Workforce Development (OSWD) was created as part of a $350 million workforce development investment announced by Governor Kathy Hochul in April 2022, and is charged with aligning workforce programs to employer needs and creating opportunities for unemployed, underemployed and underrepresented workers.

ESD has identified Artificial Intelligence as one of the state's highest-growth sectors, pointing to Cornell Tech research, companies using AI for analytics and automation, and state-backed initiatives such as Empire AI.

ESD's stated pain point is that rapid AI advancement risks widening economic inequality, because many well-paying AI jobs require specialized education and technical training that lower-income New Yorkers cannot access.
ESD also cites tech recruiting practices that favor students at elite schools and those with personal connections to prominent technology companies as a barrier AI Prep is meant to level.

The procurement is subject to a Procurement Lobbying Law restricted period running until contract approval, during which bidders may contact only the designated contacts (Julia Borukhov, primary; Jordan Kaplan, secondary) by email at AI.Prep@esd.ny.gov.

goal.text: ESD seeks to award contracts to up to two qualified program administrators to develop the curriculum for and administer the AI Prep applied training program, covering Track A and/or Track B.

Track A, "AI Prep 4 Internships," requires the administrator to deliver a comprehensive AI technology training program for low-income matriculating undergraduates, including paid internship placements at leading New York tech companies leading ultimately to full-time jobs.

Track B, "AI Prep 4 Jobs," requires an accelerated training or bootcamp alternative to degree programs that equips low-income New Yorkers with barriers to employment with in-demand AI technical and professional skills and connects them to full-time AI jobs.

Both tracks must include targeted outreach and recruitment, an application and assessment process, industry-informed online AI curriculum, participant stipends and wrap-around supports such as mentors or success coaches, and employer relationship-building to generate placements.

The selected administrator(s) will operate the program over an initial term of up to 18 months, with possible renewal or extension based on performance, need and availability of funds, and an anticipated contract start date of January 1, 2026.

Awarded administrators must track and report data including applicant, enrollment and completion counts with low-income percentages, paid internship and full-time job placement rates, and participating colleges and employer partners, with the exact list set during contract negotiation.

success_criteria.text: Proposals are scored out of a maximum of 100 points by an ESD selection committee, allocated as Firm Qualifications 15, Experience 25, Project Plan 30, Cost of Services 20 and Diversity Practices 10.
The program must serve a minimum of 250 participants, with priority for applicants proposing to serve more than 400 participants, and over 50% of participants must be low-income.
The majority of program graduates must secure paid internships or full-time employment in artificial intelligence or a closely related field.

The Project Plan must include a monthly timeline through first-cohort placement, proposed training duration, cohort size, stipend level, and estimated annual performance against three metrics: total participants served, percentage of low-income participants completing the curriculum, and placement rate.
The Project Plan must be supported by 1-page resumes of key personnel and letters from partner employers committing to provide paid internships or full-time employment to graduates.
Questions are due by August 29, 2025, ESD answers are due September 12, 2025, and proposals must be submitted by 2:00 PM ET on October 1, 2025, with award announced November 14, 2025.

Proposals must be uploaded as a main folder named "company name – RFP title – date of Submission" containing separate Administrative and Technical Proposal subfolders to the Dropbox at https://www.dropbox.com/request/AIPrep; fax, hardcopy and email submissions are not accepted and late proposals will not be considered.

constraints.text: ESD will invest up to $2M per track (up to $4M total), and budgets exceeding $2M for one track or $4M for both tracks over the total contract period will not be considered.

Indirect costs are not an allowable cost under this grant, and the budget must be mapped to the program duration across Staff Salary and Benefits, Wraparound Supports and Participant Stipends, and other program costs such as curriculum development, marketing and events.
There is no cost-match requirement, but applicants can earn additional scoring points for cost matching, which must be indicated in the budget template.

Applicants must be non-profit or for-profit entities with experience in at least three of four domains: academic services to college students, high-tech accelerated training programs, serving low-income populations, and working in the New York market.
The resulting contract carries a 30% MWBE participation goal and a 6% SDVOB participation goal, with MWBE and SDVOB Utilization Plans (OCSD-4) required and good faith efforts documented.

The selected contractor must carry Commercial General Liability of $1M per occurrence and $2M aggregate, Sexual Abuse and Molestation insurance of $1M, statutory Workers' Compensation and Disability coverage, and name ESD as additional insured with a waiver of subrogation.

Appendix A (ESD IT Security Standard Brief) and Appendix B (Diversity Practices Questionnaire) are referenced by the RFP but their content is not included in the RFP text, so bidders must obtain them separately.

Contractor staff are subject to ESD approval, staff continuity is expected through project completion, and no subcontracting is permitted unless indicated in the proposal and approved in writing by the State Project Manager.

The client is Empire State Development ("ESD" or the "Corporation"). ESD's mission is to promote a vigorous and growing state economy, encourage business investment and job creation, and support diverse, prosperous local economies across New York State. It does this through the efficient use of loans, grants, tax credits, real estate development, marketing, and other forms of assistance.

In April 2022, Governor Kathy Hochul announced a $350 million investment for workforce development, including creation of the Office of Strategic Workforce Development (OSWD) within ESD; OSWD is charged with aligning workforce development efforts with employers' needs and priorities and helping create economic opportunities for unemployed, underemployed, and underrepresented workers while meeting labor needs of the state's highest-growth sectors. One such sector is Artificial Intelligence (AI), which is advancing rapidly and revolutionizing industries such as healthcare, finance, transportation, and manufacturing. New York State is described as a key hub for AI development, with institutions like Cornell Tech leading research, companies leveraging AI for data analytics, automation, and decision-making, and state-backed initiatives like Empire AI supporting AI-driven advancements in medicine, infrastructure, and cybersecurity. The document states that rapid AI advancement raises concerns about widening economic inequality, particularly for low-income individuals who may lack the skills or access needed to benefit from the AI-driven economy, since many well-paying AI-related jobs require specialized education and technical training often out of reach for lower-income individuals. By implementing AI Prep, New York intends to create opportunities in this sector while reinforcing its position as a hub for innovation and economic opportunity.

Under Governor Hochul's direction, OSWD is launching AI Prep, an applied training program aimed at expanding access to the specialized skills and opportunities needed for AI jobs. The program responds to tech recruiting practices that favor students at elite schools and those with personal connections to prominent technology companies; AI Prep aims to level the playing field by training low-income New Yorkers in cutting edge AI skills with the goal of connecting them with AI internships or jobs at leading New York tech companies. AI Prep has two dedicated tracks for New Yorkers currently underrepresented in the tech industry who cannot reasonably access training on their own: Track A, "AI Prep 4 Internships," provides low-income matriculating undergraduate students with AI training with the goal of securing paid internship opportunities at leading tech companies; Track B, "AI Prep 4 Jobs," connects low-income New Yorkers with barriers to employment with AI jobs through an accelerated training or bootcamp that serves as an alternative to traditional degree programs. OSWD seeks to award contracts to up to two (2) qualified program administrators to develop the curriculum for and administer AI Prep for Track A and/or Track B.

Track A: AI Prep 4 Internships — the administrator must develop and deliver a comprehensive AI technology training program for low-income college students that includes paid internship placements, creating direct pathways from education to the AI industry and building a talent pipeline for AI employers. Administrator responsibilities include: targeted outreach and recruitment strategy for low-income students; a program application and evaluation process; needs assessments to identify and address student barriers; industry-informed AI curriculum design; delivery and management of the AI training program; participant stipends and wrap-around supports including mentorships and career coaches with industry expertise; and helping students secure paid internships. The administrator must also cultivate and maintain relationships with leading industry employers to inform training content and generate paid internship opportunities. The curriculum should consist of online AI courses developed with input from leading researchers and industry experts, with mentorship and real-world machine learning projects; the administrator should propose whether training is offered during the academic year or through summer courses, demonstrating alignment with employer internship hiring cycles/needs. Training should be tailored to help students secure paid internship placements with leading New York State technology companies, leading ultimately to full-time jobs.

The administrator must deliver an industry-informed, comprehensive AI technology training program equipping low-income New Yorkers with barriers to employment with in-demand technical and professional skills and connecting them to AI jobs. Required program elements: tailored outreach and recruitment strategy for unemployed, underemployed, and underrepresented New Yorkers; online AI courses with curriculum incorporating industry input on technical skills and learning milestones; a program application and assessment process; an immersive training schedule deliverable part-time or full-time; participant stipends and wrap-around supports including success coach staff; evaluation metrics for participant skill attainment during training; professional development support throughout training; credentials expected upon completion (if applicable); and full-time job connection support in an AI-related field. The administrator is expected to cultivate and maintain relationships with leading industry employers to inform training content and generate full-time employment opportunities. ESD will invest up to $2M for each track (up to $4M total) to train and provide stipends for participants, with an initial term of up to 18 months and possible renewal or extension based on performance, need, and availability of funds.

ESD anticipates selecting up to two program administrators to design and deliver the AI Prep program. Program objectives: serve a minimum of 250 participants, with priority for applicants serving more than 400 participants; over 50% of participants should be low-income; the majority of graduates should secure paid internships or full-time employment in artificial intelligence or a closely related field. Applicants must be organizations with a strong track record for workforce development in AI or similar fields. Applicants may form teams to increase competitiveness, but one organization must be the lead for the proposed programming.

Applicants to administer the program may be either non-profit or for-profit entities. Applicants must have experience in at least three of four domains to qualify: providing academic services to college students; administering high-tech accelerated training programs; serving low-income populations; working in the New York market.

ESD will fund up to an 18-month period for the selected administrator(s) to operate the AI Prep program. Applicants must detail their own budget and associated justification. Budgets exceeding $2M for one track or $4M for both tracks for the total contract period will not be considered. ESD has the right to review all expenses and deny reimbursement of any expenses deemed ineligible.

Applicants must submit a proposed budget mapped to the program duration, comprising: Staff Salary and Benefits; Wraparound Supports and Proposed Participant Stipend Level; and other costs deemed necessary for program success, including but not limited to curriculum development and implementation, marketing, and events. Indirect costs are not an allowable cost under this grant.

The grant has no cost-match requirement. Applicants can receive additional points during the scoring process for cost-matching. The extent of cost matching should be indicated in the budget template. A footnote states the proposed definition is eligible for, or in receipt of, Pell Grants, but applicants may propose and offer justification for an alternative definition.

Applicants awarded funding must track and record information relevant to the success of this grant, and data will be made available to ESD as requested. Data points to be captured and tracked are at the discretion of ESD, with the exact list determined during the contract negotiation process. Expected data points include: number of applicants, including the percentage that are low-income; number of participants who enroll, including the percentage that are low-income; number of participants who complete the program, including the percentage that are low-income; paid internship placement rate, including the percentage of placements for low-income students; full time job placement rate, including the percentage of placements for low-income individuals; participating colleges and universities; and participating employer partners.

The RFP anticipates contract award on the following schedule: Release of RFP August 8, 2025; Deadline for Submission of Questions August 29, 2025; Deadline for ESD to Respond to Questions September 12, 2025; Submission of Proposals October 1, 2025 by 2:00 PM ET; Interviews (if necessary) first week of November 2025; Announcement of Successful Respondent November 14, 2025; Anticipated Contract Start Date January 1, 2026; Anticipated Debriefing Timeframe TBD. The Corporation reserves the right to change any of the dates stated in this RFP.

ESD shall establish a selection committee to evaluate Proposals. The selection committee will consider stated criteria and assign point values to each Proposal based on their evaluation. The maximum number of points any Proposal may receive is 100.

Section VI.A "Firm Qualifications" is worth 15 points in the Technical Proposal. Respondents must include a cover letter describing the organization's mission and history, annual budget, annual number of participants served, partnerships with employers, and motivations for applying to run AI Prep. Respondents must also describe how their organization delivers substantive, skill-based, college-level or accelerated immersive training in AI, which industry experts they partner with, and how they ensure the curriculum remains current and aligns with employer demand.

Section VI.B "Experience" is worth 25 points of the selection criteria. Respondents must demonstrate knowledge and ability to perform the RFP services by describing: work with college students (if applicable), detailing length of training, number of students served, number of cohorts, cost per student, and internship and/or job placement rates of recent program graduates. They must also describe work training a high-tech workforce in AI and related fields excluding college students, with length of training, number of participants served, number of cohorts, cost per participant, and job placement rate of recent program graduates. Respondents must describe work with low-income students or individuals, including number served and any additional supports provided; how the organization coordinates with individual employers to place participants in AI-related internships or jobs; and any work in the New York market.

Section VI.C "Project Plan" is worth 30 points of the Technical Proposal. Respondents must describe how their organization would administer the AI Prep program, including a monthly timeline for planning and administering the program through completion of internships or full-time jobs by the first cohort, covering: curriculum development (or specify if already completed); recruiting participants for Track A or Track B; proposed training duration; proposed cohort size; proposed stipend level and/or other supports offered; and internship or full-time job placement. Respondents must describe how AI Prep funding will expand similar programming currently offered, how many additional participants they could serve, and how they will maintain or enhance quality of current programming; if applying for both Tracks, provide a detailed description of organizational capacity and strategy to manage two programs simultaneously per the RFP's expectations. Required attachments: 1-page resumes of key personnel involved in administering the program, and letters from partner employers demonstrating commitment to providing paid internships or full-time employment to graduates. Recruitment section must define low-income for the purposes of the program, describe how recruitment would be targeted for the applicable Track(s), and include details on partnerships with nonprofits and any New York colleges or universities.

This chunk is part of the "C. Project Plan (30 Points)" selection criterion. It asks proposers to include details on any relevant partnerships with nonprofits and any New York colleges or universities. It asks proposers to describe how they currently measure and report program success and to estimate annual performance against three metrics, justifying responses based on historical experience and/or commitments from proposed program partners: total number of participants served annually; percentage of low-income participants that complete the curriculum; paid internship or full-time job placement rate of program graduates.

Cost of Services is worth 20 Points in the Selection Criteria. Respondents must submit a line-by-line price proposal of proposed fees to accomplish the scope of work in this section of the Technical Proposal. Personnel Services (PS) costs must include job title, name of employee (if known), hourly rate or annual compensation rate, fringe rate, percentage of time dedicated to project, and cost to contract. Other Than Personnel Services (OTPS) costs must be listed on separate lines with cost to contract and number of each item; examples given are hardware/equipment, software, training materials, insurance, participant stipends, and wrap-around services such as transportation assistance. A bracketed note states that in case of complex cost structure, the originator should establish a uniform schedule inclusive of all fee components.

The chunk states that ESD (Empire State Development) is required, pursuant to New York State Executive Law Article 15-A and Parts 140-145 of Title 5 of the New York Codes, Rules and Regulations, to promote opportunities for maximum feasible participation of New York State-certified Minority and Women-owned Business Enterprises ("MWBEs") and the employment of minority group members and women in the performance of ESD contracts. It is a contractual requirement under the section "Non-Discrimination and Contractor & Supplier Diversity Requirements."

ESD establishes an overall goal of 30 percent for MWBE participation in this solicitation, based on current availability of MBEs and WBEs. A Contractor on any resulting Contract must document good faith efforts to provide meaningful participation by MWBEs as subcontractors and suppliers; by submitting a response, the Respondent agrees ESD may withhold payment pending receipt of required MWBE documentation. The MWBE directory is at https://ny.newnycontracts.com and guidance on evaluating "good faith efforts" is in 5 NYCRR § 142.8. Only sums paid to MWBEs for a commercially useful function (as defined in 5 NYCRR § 140.1) count toward the goal; for construction contracts an MWBE supplier counts as 60 percent of total contract value and a broker as the monetary value of fees or markup percentage, while for all other contracts an MWBE broker counts as 25 percent of total contract value.

Chunk sets MWBE participation compliance rules for contracts resulting from this RFP. For all other contracts, the portion of a contract with an MWBE serving as a broker deemed to represent the commercially useful function performed by the MWBE is 25 percent of the total value of the contract. Per 5 NYCRR § 142.13, a finding that the Respondent willfully and intentionally failed to comply with MWBE participation goals constitutes a breach of contract and ESD may withhold payment as liquidated damages, calculated as the difference between (1) all sums identified for payment to MWBEs had the Contractor achieved the contractual MWBE goals and (2) all sums actually paid to MWBEs for work performed or materials supplied under the Contract. By submitting a proposal, a Respondent agrees to demonstrate good faith efforts to achieve applicable MWBE participation goals by submitting evidence through the New York State Contract System ("NYSCS") at https://ny.newnycontracts.com, or via a non-electronic method by contacting the Office of Contractor and Supplier Diversity ("OCSD") at OCSD@esd.ny.gov. Respondents must submit an MWBE Utilization Plan with their proposal; modifications or changes to an accepted plan after Contract award and during the Contract term must be reported on a revised MWBE Utilization Plan submitted to ESD for review and approval, and ESD will advise of acceptance or issue a notice of deficiency within 30 days of receipt.

ESD reviews the submitted MWBE Utilization Plan and advises the Respondent of acceptance or issues a notice of deficiency within 30 days of receipt. If a notice of deficiency is issued, the Respondent must respond within seven (7) business days by submitting a written remedy to OCSD at OCSD@esd.ny.gov; if the remedy is untimely or inadequate, ESD directs the Respondent to submit a request for partial or total waiver of MWBE participation goals within five (5) business days, and failure to file the waiver form timely may be grounds for disqualification. ESD may disqualify a Respondent as non-responsive if it fails to submit an MWBE Utilization Plan, fails to submit a written remedy to a notice of deficiency, fails to submit a request for waiver, or if ESD determines the Respondent failed to document good faith efforts. The successful Respondent must attempt in good faith to utilize any MBE or WBE identified in its MWBE Utilization Plan during Contract performance; waiver requests after Contract Award may be made at any time during the Contract term but no later than prior to submission of a request for final payment. The successful Respondent must submit a quarterly MWBE Contractor Compliance & Payment Report to ESD by the 10th day following each end of quarter over the Contract term documenting progress toward the MWBE goals.

By submitting a proposal, the Respondent agrees to the terms of SCHEDULE B - PARTICIPATION BY MINORITY AND WOMEN-OWNED BUSINESS ENTERPRISES: REQUIREMENTS AND PROCEDURES. The Respondent must ensure that it and any subcontractors awarded a subcontract for the construction, demolition, replacement, major repair, renovation, planning or design of real property and improvements thereon (the "Work") undertake or continue programs ensuring minority group members and women are afforded equal employment opportunities without discrimination because of race, creed, color, national origin, sex, age, disability or marital status, applying to recruitment, employment, job assignment, promotion, upgrading, demotion, transfer, layoff, termination, and rates of pay or other compensation. This requirement does not apply to (i) work, goods, or services unrelated to the Contract or (ii) employment outside New York State. The Respondent must submit a Minority and Women-owned Business Enterprise and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement, OCSD-1, to ESD with its proposal. If awarded a Contract, the Respondent must submit a Workforce Utilization Report and require each Subcontractor to submit one quarterly during the Contract term in the format required by ESD; pursuant to Executive Order #162, contractors and subcontractors must also report gross wages paid to each employee for work performed on the contract via the Workforce Utilization Report quarterly.

Contractors and subcontractors must report gross wages paid to each employee for work performed on the contract using the Workforce Utilization Report on a quarterly basis, pursuant to Executive Order #162. Under Article 15 of the Executive Law (the "Human Rights Law") and other State and Federal statutory and constitutional non-discrimination provisions, the Contractor and subcontractors must not discriminate against employees or applicants on the basis of race, creed (religion), color, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, military status, age, disability, predisposing genetic characteristic, marital status or domestic violence victim status, and must follow the Human Rights Law regarding prior criminal conviction and prior arrest. Failure to comply may result in a finding of nonresponsiveness, non-responsibility and/or breach of the Contract, leading to withholding of funds, suspension or termination of the Contract or other enforcement proceedings. Required forms referenced: Form OCSD-1 (Policy Statement), OCSD-2 (Staffing Plan), OCSD-3 (Workforce Utilization Report), OCSD-4 (Utilization Plan), OCSD-5 (Waiver Request Form), OCSD-6 (Compliance Report), available at esd.ny.gov links or by request from OCSD@esd.ny.gov.

ESD has determined, pursuant to New York State Executive Law Article 15-A, that assessment of Respondents' diversity practices is practical, feasible, and appropriate. Respondents must include the Diversity Practices Questionnaire (see Appendix B) as part of their response to this procurement. The chunk references Appendix B, a document provided separately.

Article 3 of New York State Veterans' Services Law provides for meaningful participation in public procurement by certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Businesses ("SDVOB"). ESD recognizes the need to promote employment of service-disabled veterans and to ensure certified service-disabled veteran-owned businesses have opportunities for maximum feasible participation in the performance of ESD contracts. Respondents are expected to consider SDVOBs in fulfilling the requirements of the Contract, including as subcontractors or suppliers, as protégés, or in other partnering or supporting roles.

ESD establishes an overall goal of 6% for SDVOB (Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Business) participation, based on the current availability of qualified SDVOBs. Respondents/Contractors should reference the directory of New York State Certified SDVOBs at https://online.ogs.ny.gov/SDVOB/search. Questions regarding compliance with SDVOB participation goals should be directed to the Designated Contacts. Following Contract execution, the Contractor is encouraged to contact the Office of General Services' Division of Service-Disabled Veterans' Business Development at 518474-2015 or VeteransDevelopment@ogs.ny.gov to discuss methods of maximizing SDVOB participation. The Contractor must document "good faith efforts" to provide meaningful participation by SDVOBs as subcontractors or suppliers in performance of the Contract.

Respondents must submit a completed SDVOB Utilization Plan on Form OCSD-4 in accordance with 9 NYCRR § 252.2(i). The Utilization Plan must list the SDVOBs the Respondent intends to use to perform the Contract, a description of the work the SDVOB will perform to meet the Contract goals, and the estimated dollar amounts to be paid to an SDVOB or, if not known, an estimate of the percentage of Contract work the SDVOB will perform. Signing the plan acknowledges that false representations or information showing a lack of good faith are prohibited by law and may result in penalties including termination for cause, loss of eligibility to submit future bids or proposals, and/or withholding of payments. Any modifications or changes to agreed SDVOB participation after Contract award and during the Contract term must be reported on a revised SDVOB Utilization Plan submitted to ESD. ESD will review the plan and advise the Respondent/Contractor of acceptance or issue a notice of deficiency within 20 days of receipt.

ESD reviews the submitted SDVOB Utilization Plan and advises the Respondent/Contractor of acceptance or issues a notice of deficiency within 20 days of receipt. If a notice of deficiency is issued, the Respondent/Contractor must respond within seven business days of receipt with a written remedy; if the remedy is untimely or inadequate, ESD directs submission of a request for partial or total waiver of SDVOB participation goals on OCSD-5 within five business days of ESD notification, and failure to file the waiver form timely may be grounds for disqualification. ESD may disqualify a proposal as non-responsive if the Respondent fails to submit an SDVOB Utilization Plan, fails to submit a written remedy to a notice of deficiency, fails to submit a request for waiver, or if ESD determines the Respondent failed to document good faith efforts. If awarded a Contract, the Contractor certifies it will follow the submitted SDVOB Utilization Plan for performance of SDVOBs pursuant to the prescribed SDVOB contract goals. Failure to use SDVOBs as agreed in the Utilization Plan constitutes a material breach, entitling ESD to any remedy provided, including a finding of Contractor non-responsibility.

Respondents/Contractors seeking a partial or total waiver of goal requirements must first speak to the Designated Contacts at ESD for guidance. Under 9 NYCRR § 252.2(m), a Respondent/Contractor able to document good faith efforts to meet the goal requirements (set forth in clause IV) may submit a waiver request on Form OCSD-5 with supporting documentation; a Respondent may submit the waiver request at the same time it submits its SDVOB Utilization Plan, and if not accepted by ESD at that time, clauses II (C), (D) & (E) apply. If the waiver documentation is complete, ESD shall evaluate the request and issue written notice of acceptance or denial within 20 days of receipt. The Contractor shall attempt in good faith to utilize the SDVOBs identified in its SDVOB Utilization Plan during contract performance; waiver requests made after contract award may be made at any time during the contract term to ESD but no later than prior to submission of a request for final payment on the Contract.

Requests for partial or total waiver of established goal requirements made after Contract award may be submitted to ESD at any time during the Contract term, but no later than prior to submission of a request for final payment on the Contract. If ESD reviews the SDVOB Utilization Plan and Monthly SDVOB Compliance Report (OCSD-6) and determines the Contractor is failing or refusing to comply with contract goals with no waiver issued, ESD may issue a notice of deficiency. The Contractor must respond to the notice of deficiency within seven business days of receipt; the response may include a request for partial or total waiver of SDVOB contract goals. Waiver requests should be sent to OCSD.

Chunk sets out required good faith efforts documentation for utilizing SDVOBs on the Contract, per 9 NYCRR § 252.2(n). Evidence must include: (1) copies of solicitations to SDVOBs and any responses; (2) explanation of specific reasons each responding SDVOB was not selected; (3) dates of any pre-proposal, pre-award or other meetings attended by Contractor, if any, scheduled by ESD with certified SDVOBs ESD determined capable of fulfilling the SDVOB goals set in the Contract; (4) information describing specific steps undertaken to reasonably structure the Contract scope of work for subcontracting with, or obtaining supplies from, certified SDVOBs; (5) other information deemed relevant to the waiver request. The section concerns New York State-certified Minority and Women-Owned Business Enterprises and equal employment opportunities for minority group members and women.

Contractor must report Monthly SDVOB Contractor Compliance to ESD during the term of the Contract, covering the preceding month's activity and documenting progress toward the Contract SDVOB goals, per 9 NYCRR § 252.2(q). The report must use form OCSD-6, available on the ESD website, completed by the Contractor. It must be submitted to ESD by the 10th day of each month during the Contract term, for the preceding month's activity, to OCSD@esd.ny.gov.

The chunk is section X.ix "Encouraging the Use of NYS Businesses in Contract Performance Form" of an ESD contract for commodities, services or technology. Respondents are strongly encouraged and expected to consider New York State businesses in fulfilling the contract requirements. ESD requests that each Respondent complete the Encouraging Use of New York State Businesses in Contract Performance form, accessible at https://esd.ny.gov/sites/default/files/media/document/USEOFNYSBUSINESSES2025.pdf, so ESD can assess the use of New York State businesses in each Proposal.

Contracts resulting from this solicitation are subject to State Tax Law Section 5-a (STL 5-a), which prohibits ESD from approving a contract with an entity (or its affiliates, subcontractors, or subcontractors' affiliates) that makes sales in New York State of tangible personal property or taxable services over $300,000 and is not registered for sales and compensating use tax purposes. All Respondents must include a properly completed Form ST220-CA (http://www.tax.ny.gov/pdf/current_forms/st/st220ca_fill_in.pdf) or an affidavit (https://esd.ny.gov/sites/default/files/media/document/STL5A-Affidavit-2025.pdf) that the Respondent is not required to be registered with the State Department of Taxation and Finance. Proposals without a properly completed ST-220-CA will be considered incomplete and non-responsive and will not be considered for contract award; contracts will require periodic updating of the certifications in Form ST-220-CA. Only the prime consultant must complete Form ST 220-CA, but Schedule A to Form ST 220-TD requires detailed sub-consultant information such as tax ID number, if applicable, and certificates of authority must be attached by the prime consultant and all subconsultants if applicable.

ESD will prepare a contract after final selection of a Respondent, defining all project terms and conditions and the Respondent's responsibilities in conformance with Schedule A. A sample Schedule A is referenced at https://esd.ny.gov/sites/default/files/ScheduleA-Services_Materials-3818.pdf. Respondents must not submit the information/documentation required by Schedule A with their proposal, aside from information otherwise required by this solicitation. Respondents must thoroughly review Schedule A terms, which are standard for all ESD contracts, and submit any concerns in writing with the Respondent's Administrative Proposal; failure to submit concerns in a timely manner is deemed a waiver of objections, and successful Respondents must accept the Schedule A terms in the executed contract.

The selected Respondent must provide, at minimum and to the extent applicable: Commercial General Liability of $1 million per occurrence and $2 million in the aggregate; Commercial Automobile insurance with a limit of not less than $1 million if a vehicle is used in business; Sexual Abuse and Molestation Insurance of $1 million; Worker's Compensation & Employer's Liability insurance at State statutory limits; and Disability insurance coverage at State statutory limits. NYS Urban Development Corporation d/b/a Empire State Development (ESD) must be named as additional insured on a primary and non-contributory basis on the Commercial General Liability and Auto Liability policies. All policies above should include a waiver of subrogation in favor of ESD.

Proposers must provide a completed W-9 form and submit it with the proposal. The form is the IRS W-9 at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fw9.pdf. This appears under section X. CONTRACTUAL REQUIREMENTS, item xiv. W-9 Form.
